tickets.title: Unattended service: the owner switches it on for chosen Objectives and their ticket queues keep moving
tickets.what: Spec §2.1 (26.02), D-2026-11-26-02, owner 2026-11-26: an unattended service the owner sets up and switches on explicitly, never inferred from activity or presence. `hud unattended on --objective <id> [--objective <id>...]`, `off`, `status` (and the same toggle in panel Settings). While on, one resident service per machine (exact PID + start recorded in HUD_HOME; one instance; survives the main session and MCP closing) starts the ticket-queue workflow run (workflow/05) for each chosen Objective's ready tickets, starts a new run when tickets become ready, and lets runs end with the `lead` acceptance (workflow/07): the lead answers worker questions within its authority, repairs failures, runs the milestone reviewer, accepts owner-try items as main does today, and lands. It never opens new Objectives, never edits `docs/spec.md`. Hand-back (owner's choice): only an item that would delete a user-visible feature or change the spec stops; it becomes an owner request on Home and the service continues with other items. Off stops starting new runs and lets running jobs finish (no kill). Home shows one line while it is on (Objectives, running count, open hand-backs); the bar shows a compact marker. Results and hand-backs are what the owner reads on return; no activity tracking.

acceptance.text: Tests (fake herdr/CLIs): on with one Objective runs its two ready tickets in one Objective run (N + 2 sessions) to landed with the dispatcher's main session gone; a held ticket (unapproved removal or spec change) stays on Home and excludes its dependents while an unrelated ready ticket in the same Objective run still lands; off starts nothing new and kills nothing
One instance per machine: a second `on` updates the chosen Objectives instead of starting another service; status reports PID, Objectives, runs and hand-backs
Owner try: switch it on for a small Objective with two or three tickets, close the main session, come back to landed results and any hand-back on Home

tickets.title: Unattended trial 2: scope assumptions go to a lead; unattended runs can be cancelled
tickets.what: Main's second live trial 2026-11-26 (~/projects/hud-unattended-trial, run q9a4a94e1712eecb8). (1) A correct job (jd12cabdcb50ccc21) wrote `Assumed: scope — the requested wording replaces the old greeting text without removing the greeting feature.` and the assumption breaker held it for the owner. Workers label assumptions `scope` freely, so under the unattended escalation rule (owner hand-back only for visible deletion or spec change) a scope-tagged assumption, or more than three assumptions, goes to a temporary one-decision lead that answers continue (the item lands) or hold (with a reason that names deletion/spec, else repair); only the lead's deletion/spec verdict becomes an owner hold. Runs whose hand-back goes to main keep today's breaker. (2) There is no way to cancel an unattended run: `hud_tickets run cancel` filters unattended receipts out (src/mcp/ticket-queue.ts:59-60) and `cancelTicketQueue` only stops `working` runs, so main had to edit two paused receipts by hand. Add `hud unattended cancel <run>` (and accept it from main's `hud_tickets run cancel` with the run id) that cancels a working or paused run without signalling any process, leaves its holds and evidence visible, and frees the Objective for a new run. (3) `hud_tickets add` folds `what` into one line, so a `**Live try:**` written there is not on its own line; when `what` contains a `Live try:` field and no `live_try` is given, move it to the field line.

acceptance.text: Tests: scope-tagged assumption under unattended rule -> temporary lead -> continue lands; lead deletion/spec verdict -> owner hold; >3 assumptions same path; main-handback runs unchanged
Tests: cancel a paused and a working unattended run: state cancelled, no signal, holds stay, the Objective can start a new run
Live try: main reruns the synthetic trial and the clean ticket lands without an owner hold

tickets.title: Low-risk worker permission prompts are answered automatically; the rest go to main with a recommendation
tickets.live_try: none (main session verifies with a synthetic prompt in a scratch pane)
tickets.what: Owner 2026-11-26: a frontend-imp Claude pane stopped on a native permission prompt (rm of files in its own scratchpad with an unquoted variable path). HUD reported 'claude needs input in its pane' and the prompt waited for the owner. Such prompts are a typical unattended case: low-risk ones must be answered without the owner. When the watcher sees a worker (CLI or pi) waiting on a client permission prompt, HUD reads the prompt from the pane and classifies it. Low risk = the command or edit touches only the job's own worktree, task dir, scratchpad or a temp dir, is reversible or regenerable, and involves no network write, secrets, git push, install, or paths outside those roots. Low risk: HUD selects the approve option in the pane (herdr pane send-keys) and records the prompt, the decision and the reason on the job (one line in the inspector/timeline). Not low risk or unsure: the prompt goes to the main session (or the run's lead) as a job notice with the prompt text, HUD's recommendation and the exact answer action; the owner sees it only if main escalates. The classifier is the configured decision model with a fixed rule prompt and structured output (approve / hand to main, reason); without a decision model only the deterministic path check applies and everything else goes to main. Never auto-deny on the owner's behalf except a client's own timeout. Applies whether or not the unattended service is switched on (it answers for the worker, not for the owner).

acceptance.text: A synthetic pane showing a Claude Code permission prompt for `rm -f $S/*.png` where S is the job scratchpad is approved automatically within one watcher pass; the job record shows the prompt, decision and reason.

A prompt for a command outside the job roots (e.g. writing ~/.local/bin, git push, curl POST) is not answered; main gets a notice with the prompt text, a recommendation and the answer action, and answering it presses the chosen option once.
Decision-model failure or timeout falls back to the deterministic path check; anything it cannot prove low-risk goes to main.
Each pane prompt is answered at most once (idempotent across watcher restarts); a prompt that disappears before the answer is recorded as gone, not answered.
Bar and panel stop showing an auto-answered prompt as owner load; prompts handed to main are shown as main load, not owner load.
Docs: docs/reference.md and ARCHITECTURE describe the rule, the roots and the record; synthetic fixtures only.

tickets.title: Worker permission auto-approval covers every low-risk prompt the spec names, not only PNG cleanup
tickets.live_try: In a scratch herdr pane bound to a synthetic job (worktree, task dir, scratchpad, TMPDIR named after the job), show Claude Code prompts for (a) `rm -rf $S/out` inside the scratchpad, (b) `mkdir -p <worktree>/tmp/x && cp a b` inside the worktree, (c) an Edit file prompt for a file in the worktree, (d) `git push`, (e) `curl -X POST ...`, (f) `rm -f ~/.local/bin/x`: (a)-(c) are approved within one watcher pass with the decision on the job; (d)-(f) reach main as a notice with recommendation and answer action.
tickets.what: unattended/05 (6614cc5d) made automatic approval cover only `rm -f <dir>/*.png` (optionally via `S=`) with a locally proven job-owned directory (src/mcp/permission-policy.ts permissionDirectory). docs/spec.md §2.1 (D-2026-11-26-10) and the 05 ticket say any worker prompt confined to the job's own worktree, task dir, scratchpad or temp, reversible or regenerable, with no network write, secrets, git push or install, is answered for the worker. Widen the local proof to that rule while keeping 05's safety shape (no shell, no general variable expansion, symlink/realpath and uid checks, sensitive-name exclusion, re-check before keying, answer once): (1) File edit/write/create prompts (Claude `Edit file`/`Write file`/`Create file`, Codex `make the following edits`, pi equivalents) whose target path, after realpath of the nearest existing parent, is inside one of the job's roots and not under `.git/` or a sensitive name. (2) Shell commands parsed into simple commands joined by `&&`, `;` or newlines, with no pipes to shells, command substitution, redirection outside the roots, `sudo`, `eval`, `source`, or env-dumping. Allowed verbs: file housekeeping (`rm` incl. `-r/-f`, `mkdir`, `touch`, `cp`, `mv`, `ln -s` within roots, `chmod` without setuid, `tar`/`unzip` extracting into roots) and read-only or local-build tools (`ls`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `grep`, `rg`, `find` without `-delete/-exec` outside roots, `wc`, `diff`, `node`/`npm run`/`npx tsc`/`cargo build|test` with cwd in the job worktree, `git` subcommands that do not touch remotes or config: status, diff, log, show, add, commit, restore, stash, rebase within the worktree). Every path argument (and `$S`-style variables whose value is read from the worker process environment as 05 already does) must resolve inside the roots. Anything with `push`, `fetch`/`pull`/`clone`, `curl`/`wget` with a write method or upload, `npm install`/`pip install`/`cargo install`, `ssh`/`scp`, writes under `~` outside the roots, or references to key/credential files goes to main. (3) Shell cwd evidence: relative paths are allowed only when the prompt or worker process gives a verifiable cwd inside the job worktree (keep 05's rule that job.cwd alone is not evidence). (4) Decision model: send only structural facts (operation kinds, verbs, which root each path falls in, flags like recursive/force), never raw arguments, env or absolute paths; the model may move an item from approve to main but never approve something the local proof did not prove. Update the fixed rule prompt and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §5 / docs/reference.md for the changed model input. (5) Reason text names the actual proven operation (not 'regenerable PNG cleanup'). Keep everything else from 05 (ledger, notices, bar/panel load, answer path) unchanged.

tickets.title: Permission auto-approval proves the real target and binds the key press to the prompt it classified
tickets.live_try: In a scratch herdr pane bound to a synthetic job, show (a) a Claude Bash prompt `S=<scratchpad>; rm -f $S/*.png` (approved once), (b) the same prompt relying on an `S` only present in the launch environment (goes to main), (c) a multiline command preview containing a line `Bash command` (goes to main), (d) a prompt whose menu changes between capture and send (no key pressed, goes to main); restart the watcher between (a)'s send and its settle and confirm no second key press.
tickets.what: Milestone review j059e4af7ec78077e of unattended/05 (6614cc5d) found the approve path unsafe; fix it before any widening. (1) Execution-context evidence: drop the launch-environment inference of `S` (src/mcp/worker-permissions.ts:141-157, proc environ of the harness is not the tool shell); a variable is accepted only when the same command assigns it a literal path. (2) Recoverability: deletion is auto-approved only inside the scratchpad or job temp dir, or for git-tracked paths in the job worktree (recoverable from git); deletions of untracked files in the task dir or worktree go to main (an original reference image in the task dir must not pass). (3) Prompt identity: reject layouts with more than one permission heading on the visible screen or a heading inside the command/preview block; treat them as manual (main). (4) Delivery binding: immediately before `pane.send_keys`, re-read and require the same fingerprint and the same selected option; if herdr exposes a request/generation id or a conditional send, use it. (5) Ledger: an entry that ended `uncertain` or `sending` is not re-armed by a reflow to another fingerprint while the pane stays blocked; ambiguous transitions go to main for manual reconciliation; two consecutive identical prompts are distinguished by an observed unblocked state or go to main. Keep spend-before-send, the per-job lock and the private bounded ledger.

tickets.title: A run waiting for its lead's repair tickets resumes by itself once they are written
tickets.what: 2026-11-26/27, five times (chores, exec-page twice, cold-archive, nav-redesign, workflow): the lead decides repair and adds repair tickets with hud_tickets add, but the edit comes back as a queued receipt, so the accept step finds no ready tickets and the run stops with 'lead requested repair with no ready tickets'. tickets.title: Repair unattended/11: resume of a repair-job assumption pause records the approval; land records read Not done from the approved report
tickets.what: Reviewer finding raised during chores run q69ce631dff1b534b about the unattended/11 landing (0ddc8cea, d874dc5e). (a) A `handback_to: main` scope-assumption pause names the repair job (`src/mcp/ticket-queue-step.ts` ~1164-1165), but `hud_respond resume` matches only `t.job` (`src/mcp/ticket-queue.ts` ~443): the resume is reported as accepted, no approval is recorded, and the queue pauses again on the same assumption. Match the job the pause names (repair or original) and record the approval against that report signature. (b) `prepareLandRecords` reads `Not done` only from `row.job`'s report (`src/mcp/land-records.ts` ~79-91), not from the approved replacement (repair) report, so an unfinished acceptance item can be ticked. Read the report whose commit is being landed. Verify the line numbers at HEAD first.

acceptance.text: Test: a handback_to main run paused on a repair job's scope assumption resumes once on hud_respond resume and does not pause again for the same report
Test: a land after a repair ticks only acceptance items the repair report does not list under Not done
Full suite passes

tickets.title: Repair unattended/14: a lead escalation pause is answerable with hud_respond resume|stop
tickets.what: Milestone review j052818360e2b58a8 finding 1. On an ordinary lead `Decision: escalate`, `src/mcp/ticket-queue-step.ts` (~1759-1766, ~1620) leaves a failed `accept` cursor; `settleTicketHandback` (~400-414) calls `setAsking()` for blocker/assumption but not for `escalate`, so the persisted run is `paused` with choices resume/stop yet `answerTicketQueueHandback` (`src/mcp/ticket-queue.ts` ~419) refuses both with `no_pending_handback (paused for escalate)`. The main-answer escalation and repair-cap branches also store `failed` (~523, ~555). Make the step `asking` wherever resume/stop choices are offered. Resume must make forward progress (not replay the same settled lead decision): define it as main's override of the escalation (finish = accept the run, or re-dispatch a fresh lead), and take the simplest that does not loop; stop cancels as for report-gate pauses. Verify line numbers at HEAD first.

acceptance.text: Test: a run whose lead escalates (fake lead report) accepts `hud_respond resume` and moves forward without replaying the same lead decision
Test: the same run accepts `stop` and ends cancelled
Test: the repair-cap and main-answer escalation branches that offer resume/stop also leave the step asking and are answerable

tickets.title: Repair unattended/06: a pause wake is never lost to an expired typed delivery or another session
tickets.what: Milestone review j052818360e2b58a8 findings 2 and 3. (a) `src/cli/watch.ts` (~517-535, ~546-558): the Codex typed fallback claims the notice markers but stores only text and retry callback; if main has a draft or stays busy past the ten-minute guard, expiry drops the text without releasing the marker, so neither a new watcher nor `changes` can deliver the wake. Keep the claimed markers with the pending delivery and release them on expiry, cancellation or confirmed non-send; never repeat an uncertain send. (b) `src/workflows/events.ts` (~29-31, ~103-113) authorizes claiming a queue notice with `runVisible`, which allows any pane in the same project while the origin is alive (`src/workflows/scope.ts` ~10-15); another project main session can win the shared `.noticed` marker and the dispatching pane gets nothing. Keep project-wide read/control visibility, but deliver to the bound live origin; use the project fallback only when the origin is absent or dead. Verify line numbers at HEAD first.

acceptance.text: Test: a typed pause notice that expires unsent (draft present / busy past the guard) releases its marker and a later watcher pass delivers it exactly once; an uncertain send is not repeated
Test: with the origin pane alive, a second main session in the same project does not claim the run's pause notice; with the origin dead, the project fallback still delivers

tickets.title: Repair unattended/11: every automatic queue land is fenced to the judged head and report, including clean ones
tickets.what: Milestone review j052818360e2b58a8 finding 4. In `src/mcp/ticket-queue-step.ts` (~1206-1208, ~1245-1247) an ordinary item whose first report declared no blockers or triggering assumptions gets no approval fence; if its land gate fails, a repair can declare a blocker on a new report, yet `src/mcp/land-runner.ts` (~665-674) replaces `source_sha` and publishes directly. Bind every automatic ticket-queue land to the judged head and report signature (clearance counts as a judgement), so a repair that changes the commit or report returns to report triage (Blockers/Assumed gates) before publishing. Do not change the standalone manual `hud_land` route or the ordinary/unattended spec-file rules. Verify line numbers at HEAD first.

acceptance.text: Test: an ordinary-run item with a clean first report whose land repair report adds a Blockers line goes back to triage instead of publishing
Test: a land repair whose report stays clean still publishes after triage passes it
Existing land-repair and manual hud_land tests unchanged

tickets.title: Repair unattended/10: only an affirmative try-only Blockers text clears; mixed clauses go to the lead
tickets.what: Milestone review j052818360e2b58a8 finding 6. `src/mcp/report-notes.ts` (~11-12, ~48-53) treats any pending-try phrase plus detail as a try note unless a veto keyword matches, so `Blockers: owner live try remains: reopen the panel and pick which layout ships` lands without the lead. Replace the blacklist with a narrow affirmative form: the text is a try note only when it is a pending live/owner try phrase whose detail is a plain try instruction (reopen/run/check/look at ... and observe), with no second clause; anything ambiguous or mixed goes to the lead. Keep the cases ticket 10 accepted (`none requiring an owner decision.`, `none (owner live try remains)`, `owner live try remains: reopen the panel`). Remove the now-unneeded decision-keyword list (`detailNamesDecision`) if nothing else uses it.

acceptance.text: Test: `owner live try remains: reopen the panel and pick which layout ships` goes to the lead
Test: the ticket 10 clearance cases still land with the try part in run todo
Test: a try detail with a second clause joined by `and`/`;` that is not a plain observation goes to the lead

tickets.title: Repair unattended/08-09: multiple permission menus and conflicting file targets on a blocked pane go to main
tickets.live_try: In a scratch herdr pane bound to a synthetic job, show (a) a blocked pane with an earlier complete Claude permission menu still visible above the current one and (b) a Claude Edit file prompt whose heading path and question path name different directories with the same basename: each yields one main notice naming the pane and no key press.
tickets.what: Milestone review j052818360e2b58a8 findings 5 and 11, `src/mcp/worker-permissions.ts`. (5) Multiple headings defer to `unknownLayout` (~61-65), which returns null if an earlier footer is visible; with an old complete menu above the current one on a blocked pane, capture returns `unrecognized` (~311), no manual entry is written and after the queue grace it is again a generic worker problem. Multiple headings on a confirmed block must produce a manual-only (main) entry before the stale-single-menu heuristic applies. (11) In the Claude file prompt parse (~141-152) heading path and question path count as consistent when only their basenames match, even when both are qualified with different directories, and only the heading path is proved. Accept a genuinely basename-only (unqualified) display abbreviation; qualified paths that disagree make the prompt manual. Verify line numbers at HEAD first.

acceptance.text: Test: a blocked pane showing two complete permission menus yields one manual main entry and notice, no key press, and no worker failure after the grace
Test: heading `/w/a/x.ts` with question `/w/b/x.ts` is manual; heading `/w/a/x.ts` with question `x.ts` still proves the heading path

tickets.title: Repair unattended/07: permission proof narrows unproven forms to main instead of approving them
tickets.live_try: In a scratch herdr pane bound to a synthetic job, show Claude Bash prompts for (a) `S=<scratchpad>; rm -rf $S/out` (approved once), (b) the same with the worktree's `scratchpad` a symlink to a user-owned directory outside the job (main), (c) `test -d sub && cd sub; rm -f x` (main), (d) `npm run release` in the worktree (main), (e) `cp a.txt <worktree>/dir/` (main unless the derived child is proven): only (a) gets a key press; the others reach main with recommendation and answer action.
tickets.what: Milestone review j052818360e2b58a8 findings 7-10 and its deletion list, `src/mcp/permission-policy.ts`. Prefer narrowing unsupported forms to main over growing a shell interpreter; spec §2.1 approves only what is proven confined and reversible, anything unsure goes to main. (7) `resolveRoots` (~125-153) realpaths `worktree/scratchpad` and `task/scratchpad` and trusts the destination on a UID match; a symlinked scratchpad makes an outside directory a deletion root. Anchor each derived root beneath its verified job parent (realpath must stay inside it). (8) `tokenizeShell`/`proveShellPrompt` (~322-380, ~1297-1315, ~1350-1359) flatten conditionals and persist assignments/`cd` as if executed; only allow state-bearing sequences (assignment, cd) when every earlier separator is unconditional and not in a pipeline; otherwise main. (9) `validateCpMv` (~643-691) checks the destination directory, not the derived child; `validateTar`/`validateUnzip` (~773-876) do not check extracted members. Prove the effective child target (no existing symlink, recoverable or new) or send to main; tar/unzip without proven member lists go to main. (10) `npm run <script>` and `npx tsc` (~1044-1158) are not evidence of a local-only effect: hand them to main unless a trusted confined route exists (e.g. `npx --no-install tsc` with a local `node_modules/.bin/tsc` inside the worktree); arbitrary script names go to main. Delete the old PNG-only `permissionDirectory`, the root-string `permissionProof` adapter and the string branch of `normalizeProof` (~110, ~1418, ~1431); tests use the structured proof. Update docs/reference.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §5 where the approved set changes; ticket 07's acceptance item that listed `npm run build` as auto-approved is superseded by this narrowing. Verify line numbers at HEAD first.

acceptance.text: Tests: symlinked scratchpad, conditional `cd`/assignment before `;`, `cp` into a directory with an existing child symlink, tar/unzip without member list, `npm run release` and `npx tsc` without a proven local binary all go to main
Tests: `S=<scratchpad>; rm -rf $S/out`, `mkdir -p`/`cp` to explicit new targets inside the worktree and a Claude Edit file inside the worktree are still approved
The legacy string proof path is removed and no test passes a bare string as a verified proof
docs/reference.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md describe the narrowed approved set
